quotes.quote: Growth in export volumes of LPG is expected to continue in the years ahead.

terminal_growth.why: LPG export volumes are expected to keep growing, but shipping is a mature, cyclical, capital-intensive business with a ageing-fleet replacement need, so I set growth below the 3.75% anchor.

risks.risk: Freight rates collapse as 2027 newbuild deliveries arrive and Hormuz trade normalises, leaving mid-cycle margins lower than assumed
US-China port fees are reimposed and tariffs persist, cutting demand and revenue growth in the middle years

debt_level_representative.why: Debt of $853.1M is modest against about $1.9B of equity and a stated target of book leverage below 60%, and net leverage fell further to 23.5% by mid-2026.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 margin of 0.3427 is below the 2023-24 peak of 0.4277-0.4504 but near the middle of the 4-year range. 2026 is far above it: H1 operating profit was 360.0M on about 595M of shipping revenue, with spot rates at about US$74,000-88,000 per day against US$45,010 in 2025. Product Services trading profit and vessel-sale gains also sit inside operating profit, but its revenue is outside the revenue base. Both are volatile, and 2027 newbuild deliveries threaten rates.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 4.7% base-year rate is low but reflects shipping tax regimes and is close to the roughly 5% implied in H1 2026, although the filing flags tax-challenge risk.

situation.why: 2025 was a softer-rate year (spot rates down 10.9%) with a fully integrated Avance fleet, and its Product Services gross profit fell to 15.9M from 144.8M. 2026 is running well above that, helped by the Hormuz closure and longer voyages, and should not be extrapolated. I model a 2026 spike, then a fade toward a mid-cycle margin of about one-third as rates normalise and deliveries rise in 2027.

Part of this will fade as new VLGC deliveries arrive.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 4.7% rate reflects a shipping tax regime and H1 2026 tax of 17.7 million on 325 million of profit is also low, though a tax dispute could raise it.

situation.why: 2025 was a mid-cycle-to-soft shipping year with weak Product Services profit and a full year of the enlarged fleet. 2026 is already much stronger on year-to-date results, with H1 operating profit of 360 million against 138 million a year earlier. Year 1 is therefore set well above the base year and then fades toward a lower long-run margin. The revenue line leaves out Product Services, so the margin is on an unusual base and carries wide uncertainty.

business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, Shipping and Product Services.
quotes: BW LPG currently operates two segments: Shipping and Product Services.

business_model.claim: Shipping runs on a large VLGC fleet: 54 vessels owned and/or operated, including 28 owned VLGCs and 8 VLGCs owned by BW LPG India.
quotes: As of 31 December 2025, the Group owned and/or operated a fleet of 54 vessels, including 28 owned VLGCs, 8 VLGCs owned by BW LPG India, 7 time charter/bareboat in VLGCs and 7 operated VLGCs and 4 operated LGCs/MGC.

business_model.claim: Fleet scale grew through the purchase of 12 VLGCs from Avance Gas for US$1,050 million.

business_model.claim: Shipping revenue is mostly spot: 69.3% (US$703.5 million) came from spot voyages including CoAs and 30.7% (US$312.3 million) from time charters.
quotes: For the year ended 31 December 2025, 69.3% of Revenue — Shipping totalling US$703.5 million was derived from spot voyages (including CoAs), and 30.7% totalling US$312.3 million was derived from time charters.

business_model.claim: Shipping revenue depends on freight rates, the distance cargoes travel and the number of vessels available.
quotes: Revenue — Shipping depends on freight rates, the distance that cargoes must be transported and the number of vessels expected to be available at the time such cargoes need to be transported.

business_model.claim: TCE income for Shipping rose by US$100.8 million, or 16.6%, mainly because available fleet days increased.
quotes: TCE income — Shipping increased by US$100.8 million, or 16.6%, from US$608.2 million for the year ended 31 December 2024 to US$709.0 million for the year ended 31 December 2025.

business_model.claim: Spot rates are a direct revenue driver: spot voyage revenue fell mainly because of a 10.9% decline in average LPG spot rates.
quotes: This was primarily driven by a 10.9% decline in average LPG spot rates.

business_model.claim: The company tracks Shipping on a TCE basis, which is voyage revenue less voyage expenses such as fuel, port charges and commission.
quotes: TCE income – Shipping represents revenue from time charters and spot voyage charters less voyage expenses comprising primarily fuel oil, port charges and commission, and inter-segment expense.

business_model.claim: Bunker fuel is the largest voyage cost at 49% of voyage expenses, and port charges are second at 28%.
quotes: The Group’s bunker fuel expenses accounted for 49% and 47% of the Group’s voyage expenses for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Port charges accounted for 28% and 25% of the Group’s total voyage expenses for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Voyage costs fall on the company only for spot voyages; under a time charter the charterer pays them.
quotes: Under a time charter, the charterer is responsible for these costs.

business_model.claim: Most vessels trade in a pool that the company manages, and the company earns a commission on pooled vessels, including those of external participants.
quotes: The Company acts as the manager for the pool and receives a commission for all vessels that participated in the pool.

business_model.claim: Product Services buys LPG and delivers it directly to customers, with revenue of US$2,566.4 million.

For the year ended 31 December 2025, Revenue — Product Services was US$2,566.4 million.

business_model.claim: Product Services revenue comes from LPG cargo sales plus net derivative gains and losses on hedges of LPG prices and freight rates.
quotes: The Group’s revenue in Product Services is derived from trading activities, comprising the sale of LPG cargo and net derivative gains and losses, which arise from hedging transactions entered into by the Group to manage exposure to fluctuations in LPG prices and freight rates.

business_model.claim: Product Services sells under long-term supply contracts priced off a published index plus or minus a premium or discount, and also under spot sales contracts.
